# Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Nissaggiya Pācittiya 19 (Bu-Vb Np19)

**ID:** Bu-Vb Np19
**Section:** Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga (bu-vb)
**Collection:** Vinaya
**Title (Pali):** Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Nissaggiya Pācittiya 19
**Title (English, from literature):** Trading with money
**tipitaka.org (CST):** https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/vin01m.mul4.xml

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Rūpiyasaṁvohāra* Sutta constitutes the nineteenth rule in the *Nissaggiya Pācittiya* section of the *Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga* within the Pali Vinaya Piṭaka. The text sets forth the disciplinary injunction concerning commercial transactions involving currency, establishing that a Buddhist monk who receives money through trading incurs an offense that requires relinquishing the proceeds and making a formal confession (*nissaggiya pācittiya*). An English translation has been produced by Bhikkhu Brahmali.

This disciplinary rule is widely paralleled across the Vinaya traditions of other early Buddhist schools, including extant Vibhaṅga and Prātimokṣa texts of the Sarvāstivāda, Mūlasarvāstivāda, Mahīśāsaka, Mahāsaṅghika, Dharmaguptaka, and Kāśyapīya lineages preserved in Sanskrit, Chinese, and Tibetan, as well as the corresponding monastic code for nuns (such as Pali *Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga Nissaggiya Pācittiya* 22) and the *Parivāra*.
